newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada wants Security Council to handle Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Canada wants Security Council to handle Pol Pot.

text.p: Canada said on Tuesday it wanted the U.N. Security Council to sanction any move to extradite Khmer Rouge guerrilla chief Pol Pot from Cambodia so he could be tried by an international court.

"Our current position is any process to bring Pol Pot to justice should be based on the authorisation of the international community through the U.N. Security Council," Foreign Affairs spokeswoman Jennifer Ledwidge said in a telephone interview.
The Canadian stand appeared to show that the country was backing away from a U.S. request to take the lead in the extradition of Pol Pot.
"I think we're looking more at what the international effort might be ... and how Canada might be able to fit into an international effort," Ledwidge said.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright surprised Canada last weekend when she asked Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy to lead the effort to extradite Pol Pot.

Albright wanted Canada to use Canadian legislation against genocide and war crimes to demand the extradition of Pol Pot to Canada. He would then be passed to an international tribunal for the deaths of more than one million people during his brutal 1975-79 "killing fields" regime.
Canada had a team of legal experts studying the options and Prime Minister Jean Chretien was personally involved in the decision-making, government officials said.
But following the U.S. plan and using Canadian legislation to pursue Pol Pot was rife with legal problems, Ledwidge said.

Canada is concerned that no international tribunal has been set up to try Pol Pot yet. Officials are also concerned any attempt to use Canadian law to extradite him may not stand up in Canadian courts.
Canada does not have an extradition treaty with Cambodia.

The Security Council posed its own problems. China, which has a veto on the council, hinted on Tuesday that it was opposed to setting up an international tribunal for Pol Pot, who it has supported at times in the past.
"It should be decided Cambodians themselves without foreign interference," said Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai.
The Cambodian government has been adamant that Pol Pot be taken out of the country for fear of mob violence and the political repercussions of his arrest.
Cambodian government leaders have announced Pol Pot was captured by his former Khmer Rouge allies, but the West was awaiting confirmation that he was in custody.
